reason: 'Fronds spaced apart' means the parts stand well apart from others of their kind. That is FLOPO distant, the opposite of crowded.

label: epiphloeodal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a thallus by virtue of its developing on the surface of the bark on which it grows, not immersed in the bark tissue. NOTE: Lichen term; a narrower case of corticolous; opposite of endophloeodal. Probably outside PATO's scope (where an organism lives).
reason: A real lichen term for a thallus growing on top of the bark. Lichens are at the edge of FLOPO's scope, so it is kept as a low-confidence sibling of epiphytic.
Glochidiform hair tips are barbed like glochids. FLOPO barbed already has glochidiate as a synonym.

target: new: conjunction of two values (scalariform FLOPO:0991204 and fibrous FLOPO:0991026)

target: not increased thickness (PATO_0000591), at the base of the bearer
reason: The orchid lip is not thickened at its base. 'Callus' has no term (the previous review rejected it as a generic part), so this is read as negated thickness, with the base as a region of the bearer.

label: pandurate
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being fiddle-shaped: obovate, with a pair of lateral sinuses or constrictions below the middle. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991024 ovate; distinct from FLOPO:0991057 lyrate, which is pinnatifid with a large terminal lobe.
reason: A standard botanical outline shape (e.g. the banner petal) that has no term in PATO or FLOPO.
Young fern leaves coiled into a 'fist' (fiddlehead) are circinate. PATO's definition is loosely worded, but this is the intended quality.

label: herbaceous (sensu texture)
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being soft, green and pliant, neither woody nor leathery. NOTE: Not PATO:0002352 herbaceous, which is dying back to the rootstock each season; lies between FLOPO:0991046 membranous and PATO:0104010 papyraceous in the fern-frond texture series.
reason: Fern floras use 'herbaceous' as a texture of the frond, and PATO's herbaceous means a die-back life form. 'Thin' is a degree word.

target: new: conjunction of two values (scabrous FLOPO:0991058 and ciliate margin)

label: corticolous
definition: A positional quality inhering in an organism by virtue of its growing on the bark of trees or shrubs. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic; probably outside PATO's scope (where an organism lives).
reason: A habitat position like epiphytic and terrestrial, which the previous review kept in FLOPO. Used for lichens and bryophytes.
